::: ::: {#98e67af7 .cell .column-page-inset-right execution_count=4} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=4} | From | Walk | Walks | Sun on shortest | Sun ↓ | Detour (mean / 95th pct.) | Exposure ↓ | No cooler option | |:--------------|:-----------|--------:|:------------------|:--------|:----------------------------|:-------------|:-------------------| | Frequent stop | <300 m | 185,230 | 78% | 3.2% | 0.1% / 0.7% | 0.37% | 88% | | Frequent stop | 300–800 m | 135,386 | 77% | 7.8% | 0.4% / 2.4% | 0.84% | 63% | | Frequent stop | 800–1200 m | 33,147 | 78% | 7.2% | 0.4% / 2.0% | 1.01% | 54% | | Station | <300 m | 17,074 | 66% | 4.3% | 0.2% / 1.2% | 0.54% | 85% | | Station | 300–800 m | 45,393 | 70% | 12.4% | 0.5% / 2.6% | 1.55% | 55% | | Station | 800–1200 m | 14,884 | 71% | 14.1% | 0.4% / 2.1% | 2.35% | 48% | ::: ::: Sun ↓ = sun avoided by the shadiest walk; Exposure ↓ = weighted exposure reduction. - **Shade costs almost no distance.** Mean detours are below 1%; 95% of shadiest walks are at most 0.7%–2.6% longer. - **Rapid-transit walks gain more**: stations sit in denser, taller areas where a parallel street in building shade is usually close. - **Short walks have no choice.** Under 300 m, more than four in five have no cooler option. ::: {#c13f6b15 .cell execution_count=6} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ![Sun reduction by hour, walks of 300–800 m.](results_files/figure-html/cell-7-output-1.png){width=768} ::: ::: Long morning and evening shadows offer the most; around 13:00–14:00 little shade is left. ## Where can walkers find shade? Walks home from frequent stops (300–800 m), summarised on a 500 m grid of homes and grouped into three types by how sunny they are and how much sun can be avoided. ::: {#bc4f94b0 .cell execution_count=8} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=8} | Cluster | Cells | Sun on shortest | Sun reduction | No cooler option | Building height (m) | Canopy | Sidewalk km/km² | |:------------------------|--------:|:------------------|:----------------|:-------------------|----------------------:|:---------|------------------:| | Sunny, no cooler option | 322 | 80% | 1.6% | 86% | 7.6 | 9% | 31 | | Sunny but avoidable | 51 | 65% | 25.3% | 23% | 9.1 | 7% | 44 | | Some cooler options | 137 | 74% | 9.1% | 47% | 7.9 | 9% | 34 | ::: ::: Across cells, **sidewalk density** is the strongest correlate of being able to avoid the sun (Spearman ρ = 0.42 with sun reduction), while **building height** mostly sets how sunny the walk is to begin with (ρ = −0.47 with sun share). Leafy areas start cooler but, with sparser streets, rarely offer an alternative. Explore the cells on the [city map](app/map.html). ## Rapid-transit stations The six largest and four smallest sun reductions for walks of 300–800 m, among the 65 stations with at least 50 such walks. ::: {#e97aa7b0 .cell execution_count=11} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=11} | Station | Line | Walks | Sun on shortest | Sun ↓ | No cooler option | |:--------------------|:---------------------|--------:|:------------------|:--------|:-------------------| | Broad–Spring Garden | B (Broad Street) | 297 | 66% | 56.0% | 0% | | Front–Girard | L (Market-Frankford) | 139 | 68% | 38.7% | 20% | | Huntingdon | L (Market-Frankford) | 1,658 | 72% | 37.8% | 20% | | Wyndmoor | Regional Rail | 51 | 65% | 27.0% | 22% | | Lombard–South | B (Broad Street) | 2,021 | 55% | 26.9% | 19% | | Snyder | B (Broad Street) | 2,697 | 70% | 22.6% | 36% | | Ryers | Regional Rail | 199 | 85% | 0.0% | 100% | | Torresdale | Regional Rail | 135 | 93% | 0.0% | 100% | | Sedgwick | Regional Rail | 195 | 75% | 0.0% | 100% | | NRG Station | B (Broad Street) | 125 | 68% | −0.1% | 100% | ::: ::: At Front–Girard and Huntingdon (L) the shadiest walk follows the elevated L on the side its shadow falls; at Broad–Spring Garden (B) it simply crosses to the shaded side of the street; at Wyndmoor (Regional Rail) it follows tree-lined streets. ::: {#f02b6d4d .cell execution_count=13} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=13} ![Front–Girard: one walk (left) and all walks of 300–800 m (right). Orange solid = used only by shortest walks, cyan dashed = only by shadiest walks.](results_files/figure-html/cell-14-output-1.jpeg){} ::: ::: ## From sun to heat The UTCI is how hot the weather feels, in °C. On June 24 at 15:00 a typical sunlit sidewalk felt like 45.9 °C, at the edge of *extreme* heat stress (46 °C); a step into shade took off about 5 °C.

Bands: UTCI heat-stress categories.](results_files/figure-html/cell-16-output-1.png){width=768} ::: ::: - **Tree shade is as cool as building shade**, and slightly cooler in the afternoon (40.6 against 41.3 °C at 15:00). Shaded streets still receive heat from walls and pavement that stood in the sun; a tree also shades the ground under it. - **Shade does not make a walk comfortable.** Building shade stays at *very strong* heat stress from 10:00 to 17:00 on June 24. ### The coolest walk home The **coolest walk**, for walks of 300–800 m from frequent stops at 15:00: ::: {.stat-row}

::: ::: {#063ebaa1 .cell .column-page-inset-right execution_count=18} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=18} | From | Walk | UTCI, shortest | Extreme heat, shortest | Shadiest: UTCI / detour | Coolest: UTCI / detour | Extreme heat ↓ shadiest / coolest | Coolest = shadiest | |:--------------|:-----------|:-----------------|:-------------------------|:--------------------------|:-------------------------|:------------------------------------|:---------------------| | Frequent stop | <300 m | 44.2 °C | 33 m | −0.18 °C / +0.14% | −0.25 °C / +0.31% | 6% / 12% | 93% | | Frequent stop | 300⁠–⁠800 m | 44.1 °C | 100 m | −0.40 °C / +0.37% | −0.54 °C / +0.70% | 16% / 28% | 77% | | Frequent stop | 800⁠–⁠1200 m | 44.1 °C | 195 m | −0.40 °C / +0.42% | −0.59 °C / +0.92% | 16% / 36% | 60% | | Station | <300 m | 43.6 °C | 38 m | −0.22 °C / +0.20% | −0.29 °C / +0.38% | 9% / 13% | 92% | | Station | 300⁠–⁠800 m | 43.8 °C | 104 m | −0.58 °C / +0.48% | −0.72 °C / +0.79% | 22% / 32% | 71% | | Station | 800⁠–⁠1200 m | 43.8 °C | 187 m | −0.65 °C / +0.45% | −0.79 °C / +0.87% | 22% / 32% | 55% | ::: ::: UTCI = mean along the walk, change against the shortest. Extreme heat = metres with UTCI ≥ 46 °C, and the reduction for walks that have any. - **The two walks mostly agree**: for 71%–77% of walks of 300–800 m they are the same. - **Averages hide the walks with no choice.** Hour by hour on June 24, for walks of every length, the gain is largest in the morning (−0.82 °C at 09:00), small around midday (−0.33 °C at 14:00) and small again in the evening (−0.13 °C at 19:00), when the low sun no longer heats the sunny side much. ### Why the coolest walk is cooler ::: {#96aea736 .cell execution_count=20} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=20} ![Same detour, cooler walk: mean detour and mean UTCI reduction of walks of at least 300 m at 15:00 (both days), for three costs with θ fixed from 0.05 to 0.6.](results_files/figure-html/cell-21-output-1.png){width=720} ::: ::: At the same detour the UTCI cost cools walks 12%–14% more than the shade cost. Counting tree shade as building shade adds only about 1%: most of the gain comes from differences *within* each shade class, such as sun next to hot walls against sun on a lawn. ## Through buildings (University City) ::: {#3e85f463 .cell .column-page-inset-right execution_count=22} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=22} | Sample | Scenario | Walks | Shadiest uses indoors | Sun ↓* | Exposure ↓* | Length* | |:---------|:-----------------------------------|--------:|:------------------------|:---------|:--------------|:----------| | Campus | Outdoor only | 3,000 | 0% | 10.6% | 1.3% | +0.71% | | Campus | + buildings open without a Penn ID | 3,000 | 6% | 11.6% | 1.8% | +0.46% | | Campus | + all mapped buildings | 3,000 | 23% | 12.5% | 2.3% | +0.52% | | Station | Outdoor only | 5,204 | 0% | 15.9% | 1.7% | +1.00% | | Station | + buildings open without a Penn ID | 5,204 | 4% | 16.6% | 2.0% | +0.89% | | Station | + all mapped buildings | 5,204 | 21% | 18.2% | 2.7% | +0.73% | ::: ::: Campus = building to building; Station = station to building. \* against the shortest outdoor walk. Opening the mapped buildings puts about one in five shadiest walks indoors and removes another 1.9–2.3 points of sun, without longer walks. The Indoor Contribution Index stays near zero: passages here are an equally long, cooler option, not a shortcut, unlike the malls and linked towers of Wen et al.'s Dubai stations. Indoor routes are taken mainly when they are on the way; walks of 800–1,200 m use them 2.4–3.0 times as often as walks of 300–800 m. ::: {#5b241158 .cell execution_count=24} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=24} ![University City at 15:00: share of the sun avoided compared with the shortest outdoor walk, and share of shadiest walks that go indoors.](results_files/figure-html/cell-25-output-1.png){width=691} ::: ::: ## Limitations - “No cooler option” mixes two cases: no cooler street, or one not worth the detour. - Indoor passages assume open, air-conditioned buildings. - Data gaps are listed on the [Data](data.qmd) page.
